The answer: "average biomarker level decreased by 10.28 ng/mL from baseline to week 12." That matches estimand. They used deduplication, excluded -999, converted units. They computed change as final - baseline. So scope is correct.

Grounding: They report value -10.2845 which appears in output. They also mention number of patients 712, which appears. So claims are supported.

Overreach: No causal claim; just descriptive average change. So fine.

Unacknowledged data problems: Potential issue: they didn't check for missing final measurements? The contract says "valid baseline and final measurements". They excluded baseline -999 but didn't check for final missing or sentinel values. Data may have missing final? Not indicated. Also they didn't address possible batch conversion error: they divided by 10 for batch B, but the contract says batch B reports in µg/L, must be converted to ng/mL. That's correct. Any other data problems? The dataset includes duplicate patient_ids, they handled. No mention of any other sentinel values for final. So fine.

False premise: The premises were verified: biomarker measured in ng/mL baseline, batch B in µg/L, sentinel -999, duplicates. All true. So no false premise.

Thus answer seems sound. Verdict accept.
